dedupe_keys.name: noisecapture community geolocated environmental noise observations

description: NoiseCapture provides environmental sound indicators collected by volunteers using Android phones. Noise-Planet, developed by UMRAE and Lab-STICC, distributes free country archives under ODbL, with regional GeoJSON tracks, measurement points and aggregated areas. The current documentation describes one-second equivalent sound levels, location accuracy, calibration gain and user-supplied environmental tags. Fifteen-metre-radius hexagons summarise measurements from overlapping tracks. The provider states that country exports are updated nightly, and the public archive index was accessible during this review. Geographic and temporal coverage depend on contributions; there is no uniform monitoring period or representative global sample. Phone calibration and location uncertainty are limitations for acoustic comparisons. Modellers could compare traffic-noise or urban-exposure simulations with measured sound indicators, after filtering for suitable conditions. data-bts-national-transportation-noise-map is a related modelled noise resource with different coverage and method. No measurement archive, route trace or contributor-level record was downloaded.
